title: The Real AI Race: Tuya Smart Co-Founder Argues Practical Application Trumps Pure Algorithms at Summer Davos
summary: At Summer Davos 2026, Tuya Smart Co-Founder Alex Yang asserted that the future of AI competition hinges not on theoretical prowess but on tangible, real-world applications. He emphasized that companies capable of seamlessly integrating AI into practical solutions for everyday life will ultimately emerge as leaders in the evolving technological landscape.
content:
DALIAN, China — Amidst the bustling discussions at the 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions (AMNC), colloquially known as "Summer Davos," held from June 23 to 25, a potent message emerged from Tuya Smart Co-Founder and COO, Alex Yang. Speaking to a global audience of leaders and innovators, Yang laid bare a vision for artificial intelligence that cuts through the hype: the true battleground for AI supremacy lies squarely in its real-world utility, not merely in algorithmic sophistication.

Yang's compelling argument suggests a significant pivot in how we should evaluate AI's progress and competitive landscape. For years, the narrative has often centered on benchmark scores, model size, and theoretical capabilities. However, Yang contends that the companies poised to dominate the next wave of AI innovation will be those that master the art of seamless integration, transforming complex AI models into practical, user-centric applications that genuinely enhance daily life.

This perspective particularly resonates with Tuya Smart's expertise in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, where AI already powers countless smart devices. Yang underscored that the competitive edge will not go to those building the most intricate neural networks in isolation, but to those who can deploy AI to solve tangible problems, create intuitive experiences, and deliver demonstrable value to consumers and businesses alike. It’s a call to move beyond abstract potential and embrace concrete impact.

Ultimately, Yang's address at Summer Davos 2026 serves as a crucial reminder that technology's ultimate purpose is to serve humanity. As the AI arms race continues, the winners may not be the ones with the largest datasets or the most complex code, but those who can most effectively weave intelligence into the fabric of our everyday world, making it smarter, more efficient, and more responsive to our needs. The future of AI, it seems, will be decided in our homes, our offices, and our cities.
keyTakeaways: Alex Yang asserts that the future of AI competition hinges on real-world applications and practical integration, not just theoretical advancements.
Companies that excel in deploying AI to solve tangible problems and enhance daily life will lead the next wave of innovation.
The focus for AI development should shift from abstract algorithmic complexity to delivering concrete, user-centric value and seamless experience.
author: Staff Writer

title: AI's True Battleground: Tuya Co-Founder Declares Real-World Impact Over Pure Power
summary: At the 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions, Tuya Smart Co-Founder Alex Yang asserted that the future of AI competition hinges not on theoretical breakthroughs, but on practical, real-world applications. His insights emphasized a critical shift in the AI landscape towards tangible utility and widespread deployment.
content:
DALIAN, China – The bustling halls of the Dalian International Conference Center, host to the World Economic Forum's 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions (Summer Davos), buzzed with discussions on humanity's most pressing challenges and promising innovations. Among the key voices shaping the future narrative was Alex Yang, Co-Founder and COO of Tuya Smart, who offered a compelling perspective on the evolving competitive landscape of artificial intelligence.

Speaking on June 25, Yang cut through the usual AI hype, declaring that the true crucible for AI dominance lies not in abstract computational power or theoretical benchmarks, but in its ability to solve real-world problems. For too long, the narrative around AI has been dominated by ever-larger models and increasing parameter counts. Yang's message was a stark reminder that innovation only truly matters when it translates into tangible value for industries and end-users.

His vision suggests a critical pivot for companies and researchers alike. Instead of solely chasing breakthroughs in pure research, the emphasis must shift towards engineering robust, scalable, and practical AI solutions that can be seamlessly integrated into daily life and across various sectors. This includes everything from smart infrastructure and intelligent manufacturing to personalized healthcare and energy management systems. The "race to the bottom" on cost per inference, or the "race to the top" on model size, will ultimately cede to the ability to effectively deploy AI in ways that demonstrably improve efficiency, enhance experiences, and create new economic opportunities.

This isn't merely an academic observation; it's a strategic roadmap for the global AI ecosystem. Companies that can bridge the gap between cutting-edge algorithms and practical, deployable products will be the ones that win the next phase of the AI revolution. Yang's remarks at Summer Davos underscore a maturing industry vision where utility, reliability, and real-world impact are the ultimate measures of success.
keyTakeaways: The future of AI competition will be defined by practical, real-world applications, not just theoretical advancements.
Companies must shift focus from purely researching larger AI models to engineering robust and deployable solutions.
Tangible utility and seamless integration into daily life and various industries are crucial for AI's true impact and competitive edge.
author: Staff Writer
